chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Qasim al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from 'Ubayd Allah and 'Imran, the two sons of 'Ali al-Halabiyyan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If the Muzdalifah is missed by you, then the Hajj is missed by you.

key_terms.الْحَجُّ: Hajj, the major Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَةُ: Muzdalifah, a sacred site where pilgrims stand after leaving Mina, a crucial pillar of Hajj.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim misses Muzdalifah during Hajj?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting Muzdalifah as a fundamental pillar (rukn) of Hajj rather than merely a recommended act. This establishes the principle that the omission of this specific standing invalidates the pilgrimage, a view strongly supported by Shia jurists who distinguish it from other components like the Tawaf. The hadith underscores the critical timing of the night of sacrifice, linking the physical act of standing to the spiritual completeness of the rite.
